definitions.explanation: Humble form of 会う, used when the speaker is meeting someone of higher status.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}にお{目|め}にかかりたいのですが。
examples.english: I would like to meet with the president.
examples.notes: Requesting a meeting with someone important

examples.japanese: お{目|め}にかかれて{光栄|こうえい}です。
examples.english: It's an honor to meet you.
examples.notes: Polite greeting when meeting someone distinguished

examples.japanese: また{近|ちか}いうちにお{目|め}にかかりたいです。
examples.english: I hope to see you again soon.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}にお{目|め}にかかるのは{久|ひさ}しぶりです。
examples.english: It's been a long time since I last met with you, professor.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}の{会議|かいぎ}で{部長|ぶちょう}にお{目|め}にかかれると{聞|き}いて、とても{楽|たの}しみにしています。
examples.english: I heard I'll be able to meet the department head at next week's meeting, and I'm very much looking forward to it.

notes:
お{目|め}にかかる is the humble ({謙譲語|けんじょうご}) form of {会|あ}う.

KEIGO SYSTEM:
- {会|あ}う (neutral): to meet
- お{目|め}にかかる (humble): I meet [superior]
- お{会|あ}いになる (honorific): [superior] meets

CONJUGATION:
- お{目|め}にかかります (polite)
- お{目|め}にかかりたい (want to meet)
- お{目|め}にかかれて (being able to meet)

USAGE:
- Used when the speaker is the one doing the meeting
- Shows respect by lowering oneself
- Common in business and formal situations

NOTE:
- かかる is written in hiragana, not as {掛|か}かる
- The お is part of the fixed expression
